description: 27 Jan 2017. Suspended entry from Iran and six other Muslim-majority countries for 90 days. Over 700 travellers detained; up to 60,000 visas provisionally revoked, including already-issued ones.
time_note: Nominal suspension period; practical effect longer.
energy_note: Revocation of an already-granted visa mid-journey.

description: 24 Sep 2017. Suspended immigrant and most non-immigrant visas for Iranians, explicitly exempting F-1, M-1 and J-1 students. Upheld by the Supreme Court in Trump v. Hawaii, 585 U.S. 667 (2018).

aspect: The waiver that was not a waiver
description: PP 9645 provided for case-by-case waivers. Through March 2019 the State Department reported 440 waivers granted to Iranian nationals - 279 non-immigrant and 161 immigrant - out of roughly 33,900 Iranian applicants subject to the ban. Under 2%.
time_note: Waiver adjudication ran for months to years with no status.
energy_note: A process that exists on paper and almost never resolves.
source_name: US State Department waiver figures via NIAC

description: 20 Jan 2021. Biden ended PP 9645 and PP 9983 restrictions. Iranian restrictions lifted immediately, though COVID-era post closures meant practical resumption was slower.

EO 14161 (20 Jan 2025) ordered enhanced vetting and a 60-day review. Restrictions took effect June 2025. The proclamation of 16 Dec 2025, effective 1 Jan 2026, placed Iran among 19 countries under complete suspension of immigrant and non-immigrant visas. There is no separate waiver application - an applicant must apply and argue the case at interview.
energy_note: Plans built during the open window collapsed.

description: The four-year open window (2021-2025) drew people into multi-year plans - university offers, job offers, family petitions - that the December 2025 proclamation stranded. The cost is not the ban alone but the sunk investment made in reliance on its absence.
money_note: Sunk application, tuition deposit, relocation and legal spend.

description: Implementation of EO 13769 caught people already travelling: over 700 travellers were detained and up to 60,000 visas were provisionally revoked, including visas already issued and in passports.
energy_note: Lawful on departure, unlawful on arrival.

description: Reza is admitted to a PhD at Georgia Tech starting September 2026 with a funded position. On 16 December 2025 the proclamation lands.
